subject: Configural and Thresholds models with the same degrees of freedom in multigroup confirmatory factor analysis lavaan

messages.author: 706aa9301995d168
messages.subject: Configural and Thresholds models with the same degrees of freedom in multigroup confirmatory factor analysis lavaan
parts:
Hi all, 
I am conducting a multigroup confirmartory factor analysis using lavaan to test measurement invariance of a 21-items questionnaire across two groups.
Following the procedure illustrated by Svetina et al., 2019 for ordinal responses, I first fitted a configural model, then a thresholds model and compare the two. 
When I check the results I get that the two models have the same degrees of freedom and, so, they cannot be compared. Surprisingly, though, the estimated model paramters differ, with the configural model having -obviously- less parameters that the thresholds one. 
Even more surprisingly, when I fit the loadings model and compare it to the thresholds one I do get a difference in terms of degrees of freedom. It seems that something is wrong at the configural vs. thresholds models level. 
Do you have any idea of why I am encountering this issue and how I can solve it? 

Just some details:
-My sample size is N=301, distributed in 196 subs for group 1 and 106 for group 2 (I know it might be small and unbalanced). 
-I am testing a bifactor model with a general factor and 3 sub-factors.
-The response scale is 7-point Likert, thus I am treating my variables as ordinal. 
-Since some response categories where empty for some items (meaning that in one group none of the participants responded using one of the response category), I collpsed the responses category from 7 to 3. 

Here is the R script with the syntax if you want to take a look: 

bifactor.model <- '
FattoreG =~ B3 + B4 + B7+ B12 + B19 + B20 + B21 + E5 + E7 + E9 + E11 + C1 + C6 + C8  + C13 + C15 + C25 + C29 + C30 + C34 + C35
Beha  =~  B3 + B4 + B7 + B12 + B19 + B20 + B21
EmoCog =~ E5 + E7 + E9 + E11 + C1 + C6  + C15 + C30
Cog =~   C8 + C13 + C25 + C29 + C34 + C35  
'
fit.bifactPON_Region <- cfa(bifactor.model, data = dfPON.region, std.lv=TRUE,                                                                      orthogonal= T  ,ordered = names(dfPON.region[1:21]))

fitMeasures(fit.bifactPON_Region, fit.measures = c("cfi", "tli", "srmr","rmsea"), output = "matrix")

summary(fit.bifactPON_Region)

# CONFIGURAL MODEL
model.config <-  measEq.syntax(configural.model = bifactor.model,
                               data = dfPON.region,
                               ordered = names(dfPON.region[1:21]),orthogonal=T,
                               parameterization = "delta", ID.fac = "std.lv",
                               ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016",
                               group = "Target_NonTarget",group.equal = "configural")

model.baseline <- as.character(model.config)

fit.model.baseline <- cfa(model.baseline,data = dfPON.region,ordered = names(dfPON.region[1:21]),group = "Target_NonTarget")

fitmeasures(fit.model.baseline, fit.measures = c("chisq", "df", "tli", "cfi", "rmsea", "srmr"),
            output  = "matrix")

summary(fit.model.baseline)

# THRESHOLDS MODEL
model.thresholds <-   measEq.syntax(configural.model = bifactor.model,
                                    data = dfPON.region,
                                    ordered = names(dfPON.region[1:21]), orthogonal=T,
                                    parameterization = "delta", ID.fac = "std.lv",
                                    ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016",
                                    group = "Target_NonTarget",group.equal = c("thresholds"))

thresholds <- as.character(model.thresholds)

fit_thr <- cfa(thresholds, data = dfPON.region, ordered = names(dfPON.region[1:21]), group = "Target_NonTarget")

fitmeasures(fit_thr, fit.measures = c("chisq", "df", "tli", "cfi", "rmsea", "srmr"),
            output ="matrix")

# COMPARE CONFIGURAL AND THRESHOLDS MODEL 
lavTestLRT(fit.model.baseline, fit_thr)


Thank you in advance!

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Configural and Thresholds models with the same degrees of freedom in multigroup confirmatory factor analysis lavaan
parts:
Michael--
Wu and Estabrook (2016) explain what is happening. The ordinal data model includes waves of additional parameters which may be estimated, but these are not all identified--you cannot obtain unique best estimates of them--in the configural model. But if you impose equivalence of thresholds, then some of those other parameters *can* be uniquely estimated, and so, lavaan, while imposing constraints on thresholds, relaxes constraints on other parameters. Wu and Estabrook (2016) rather exhaustively illustrate different paths through the various levels of constraints that may be imposed. In addition, having only 3 response categories also puts your model into a special category regarding identification and DF. I believe there are also some lavaan tutorial resources that describe that specific situation.
Wu, H., & Estabrook, R. (2016). Identification of confirmatory factor analysis models of different levels of invariance for ordered categorical outcomes. Psychometrika, 81(4), 1014-1045.

messages.subject: Re: Configural and Thresholds models with the same degrees of freedom in multigroup confirmatory factor analysis lavaan
parts: I'll see whether get back to the original 7 responses categories solution might help or I should do something  totally different.

If you collapsed to 3 categories because all other categories were empty (at least in one of the groups), then it will not solve your problem to "add" the empty categories back.  If you only have information (in at least 1 group) to distinguish individuals into 3 categories, then you simply have to assume (not test) threshold invariance, and use that as your baseline configural model.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Dear Margaret, 
I used the collapsed categories for both models. 
To do so, I simply recoded my response values such that response values 5, 6 and 7 were recoded into 5. It's not the cleanest way, but it was the only way to solve the issue and test for measurement invariance following Svetina et al. method. 

Best wishes!

Michael

Thank you so much for your quick response! To clarify did you collapse your categories for both models, or just the thresholds one? And what algorithm did you use to collapse your categories?

On Mar 30, 2022, at 6:36 AM, 'Michael Schepisi' via lavaan <lav...@googlegroups.com> wrote:

﻿
﻿Dear Margaret, 
Yes, I solved it by collapsing my 7 response categories into 5. Collapsing into 3 gives the issue of having the baseline and the thresholds models with the same degrees of freedom. Thus, that was the only way. 
Hope it helps!

Michael

Inviato da iPhone

Il giorno 30 mar 2022, alle ore 11:36, Terrence Jorgensen <tjorge...@gmail.com> ha scritto:

﻿
I'll see whether get back to the original 7 responses categories solution might help or I should do something  totally different. 

If you collapsed to 3 categories because all other categories were empty (at least in one of the groups), then it will not solve your problem to "add" the empty categories back.  If you only have information (in at least 1 group) to distinguish individuals into 3 categories, then you simply have to assume (not test) threshold invariance, and use that as your baseline configural model.
